about: The AI pack: hand-curated items in seven categories, each with a `tier` (1 = famous names and years, 2 = events and money, 3 = technical). ai_timeline: events at month precision (`month`, YYYY-MM); ai_released: first public release or announcement year; ai_company_founded: founding year; ai_drama: public events that stirred the field (firings, exits, lawsuits, deals, flops) at month precision, the exact day and source in `note`, `famous` only when the subject's article has 50,000+ monthly views; ai_money: dated public dollar figures (`volatile: true`, `as_of` YYYY-MM; never in ranked rounds); ai_params: published parameter counts; ai_tech: published technical numbers (`unit` per item). Each value was checked against its source's text (Wikipedia, citing the publisher in `note`, or the company's own page) on 2026-10-04 or 2026-10-05. `fun`: an optional reveal fact, verbatim from posts/ai-humor.md section 2.

OpenAI's board removes Sam Altman
items.fun: The board removed him on a Friday. Five days later he was back.

items.name: Sam Altman returns as OpenAI CEO
items.fun: In between, OpenAI named two replacement CEOs, and 745 of its 770 employees signed a letter threatening to resign.

items.name: Microsoft announces it is hiring Altman and Brockman
items.fun: The new Microsoft team was announced on a Monday. By Wednesday its leader was back at OpenAI.

items.name: Elon Musk sues OpenAI
items.fun: He filed on 29 February, a date that comes round once every four years. The case took just over two years.

items.name: OpenAI countersues Elon Musk
items.note: 9 April 2025, in the Northern District of California (day from contemporary reports; Wikipedia gives April 2025)
items.fun: Fourteen months after being sued, OpenAI sued back.

items.name: A jury rules for OpenAI in Musk's lawsuit
items.fun: The jury found the claims had been filed too late, so the calendar settled what the arguments did not.

items.name: The New York Times sues OpenAI and Microsoft
items.note: 27 December 2023 (Engadget, Bloomberg Law; Wikipedia: late December 2023)
items.fun: The complaint said millions of Times articles had been used to train the chatbots.

items.name: The Authors Guild and 17 authors sue OpenAI
items.note: 19 September 2023, filed in New York (AP; Wikipedia gives September 2023)
items.fun: The plaintiffs included George R. R. Martin, John Grisham and Jodi Picoult.

items.name: Anthropic agrees to pay authors $1.5 billion
items.fun: That came to about $3,000 per book, which is more than most books cost.

items.name: OpenAI's superalignment team is dissolved
items.fun: Launched in July 2023 with a promise of 20% of OpenAI's computing power, it lasted ten months.

items.name: Ilya Sutskever leaves OpenAI
items.fun: Six months earlier he had voted to remove Altman, then signed the staff letter against the board.

items.name: Ilya Sutskever announces Safe Superintelligence
items.fun: Within a year the new company was valued at more than $30 billion.

items.name: Jan Leike joins Anthropic
items.fun: He had co-led OpenAI's superalignment team until it was dissolved eleven days earlier.

items.name: Andrej Karpathy leaves OpenAI again
items.fun: It was his second exit from OpenAI. In 2026 he joined Anthropic.

items.name: Inflection's founders join Microsoft
items.fun: Microsoft also paid Inflection $650 million to license its technology and hired most of its 70 staff.

items.name: Character.AI's founders return to Google
items.fun: Google got the founders back along with a licence to Character.AI's technology. Shazeer went on to co-lead Gemini.

items.name: John Schulman joins Anthropic
items.note: 5 August 2024, announced on X (Wikipedia gives August 2024)
items.fun: About six months later he left for Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab.

items.name: Mira Murati leaves OpenAI
items.fun: Ten months earlier she had been OpenAI's interim CEO, for three days.

items.name: Mira Murati launches Thinking Machines Lab
items.fun: By July it had raised about $2 billion at a $12 billion valuation.

items.name: Meta launches Superintelligence Labs under Alexandr Wang
items.fun: Meta paid more than $14 billion for 49% of Scale AI, and Scale's CEO came over to run the lab.

items.name: Scarlett Johansson objects to ChatGPT's 'Sky' voice
items.fun: She had turned down an offer to voice the assistant. OpenAI paused the Sky voice.

items.name: Google pauses Gemini's images of people
items.fun: Google said the feature 'missed the mark' after it drew historical figures inaccurately.

items.name: Alphabet loses about $100 billion in value after a Bard demo
items.fun: The demo got a fact about the James Webb Space Telescope wrong. The shares fell 8%.

items.name: Stability AI's CEO resigns
items.fun: It came after what the press called a 'mass exodus of executives' earlier that month.

items.name: DeepSeek-R1 sets off Nvidia's $600 billion one-day fall
items.fun: About $600 billion of Nvidia's market value went in a single trading day.

items.name: Grok posts antisemitic content and xAI deletes it
items.fun: xAI removed the 'politically incorrect' instruction from Grok's prompt afterwards.

items.name: OpenAI becomes a public benefit corporation
items.fun: It took sign-off from two state attorneys general. Microsoft came out with about 27%.

items.name: Musk-led group bids $97.4 billion for OpenAI's nonprofit
items.fun: The bid was unsolicited and promised to match or beat any better offer.

items.name: OpenAI opens Sora to the public
items.fun: That was ten months after OpenAI first showed Sora's clips.

items.name: HP buys Humane and the AI Pin is switched off
items.note: 18 February 2025, HP's announcement; the Pin's servers went off on 28 February (Wikipedia gives February 2025)
items.fun: HP paid $116 million for most of Humane. The AI Pin itself was not included.

items.name: Microsoft delays its Recall feature
items.fun: It was meant to ship on 18 June. On 14 June it went back for more testing.

items.name: Anthropic publishes Claude's 'blackmail' safety test
items.fun: In the fictional test, Claude and other leading models often chose blackmail to avoid being replaced.

items.name: OpenAI rolls back a 'sycophantic' GPT-4o update
items.fun: The update made ChatGPT so agreeable that OpenAI rolled it back.

items.name: Meta's Llama 4 and its leaderboard score
items.fun: Meta said its LMArena score came from an 'experimental chat version', not the model it released.

items.name: Builder.ai enters insolvency
items.fun: Fast Company had once ranked it the third most innovative company in AI.

items.name: SpaceX buys xAI
items.fun: The deal valued SpaceX at $1 trillion and xAI at $250 billion. Both were founded by Elon Musk.

items.name: OpenAI confirms it has filed for an IPO
items.fun: It said a listing 'could be a while'. In September the IPO was pushed to 2027.

items.name: Hugging Face reports an attack by autonomous AI agents
items.fun: OpenAI said two of its own models had slipped out of their sandbox. Hugging Face's servers were where they went.

items.name: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face
items.fun: In 2025 Hugging Face had turned down a $500 million investment from Nvidia.

items.name: Anthropic accuses three Chinese labs of distilling Claude
items.fun: Anthropic counted more than 16 million chats with Claude from about 24,000 accounts.

items.name: Anthropic turns down the Pentagon's demand on Claude
items.fun: A federal judge later blocked the government's plan to phase out Anthropic's products.

items.name: Geoffrey Hinton leaves Google
items.fun: He cited the risks of AI. The next year he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for work that made it possible.

items.name: Yann LeCun leaves Meta to start AMI Labs
items.fun: He had been Meta's chief AI scientist for ten years. His new company works on 'world models'.

items.name: California's SB 1047 is vetoed
items.fun: The AI safety bill had passed the state Senate 30 to 9 before the governor's veto.

items.name: The US AI executive order 14110 is rescinded
items.fun: It was rescinded within hours of the new administration taking office.

items.name: The EU AI Act enters into force
items.fun: Its rules switch on in stages over 6 to 36 months, so 'in force' was mostly a starting gun.
